extracted.intended_audience: early-18th-century English readers/gentlemen seeking practical advice on social behaviour, health, conversation, and dispute etiquette
extracted.subtask_description: A set of short moral and practical essays offering rules and observations for behaving at court (levées), conducting friendships and love, preserving health by temperance and exercise, and managing arguments in conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Levée-as-market-for-preferment / purpose of a levée
rubrics_metrics.description: The business of a Levée is to receive the acknowledgments of a multitude that a man is Wise, Bounteous, Valiant and Powerful; it is a Commerce between the Mighty and their Slaves, a public show in which both the Great and their followers pursue outward show rather than real happiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay treats the Levée as mostly a staged spectacle: a great man receives ostensible testimonies of respect and interest rather than genuine counsel. The representation implies that those who attend should be aware it is largely a farce and that the Levée tends to promote ostentation over business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of appearance at a levée (military vs civil)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are several ways of making the first appearance: you may be either half dressed and washing yourself (peculiar to Military Men) or reserved (the Politicians or Civil Officers preserve a certain chastity of deportment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The differing openings signal social role: military display (open-breasted, graceful exposure) versus civil reserve (buttoned up). Use of these modes conveys rank and expected decorum when presenting before a great man.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep in generals; be quick with particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: For the chief point is to keep in Generals, and if there be any thing offered that's Particular, to be in haste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At public audiences a patron should speak in generalities and avoid engaging in fine particulars; if particulars are raised, handle them hurriedly. This preserves the air of competence while enabling the patron to address many people without deep involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staging and orchestration of a levée
rubrics_metrics.description: The Levée is laid after a manner of private intimations: twenty Whispers, false Alarms, and private Intimations pass backward and forward from the Porter, the Valet, and the Patron himself before the gaping Crew are gathered; the Dumb Show is kept up by the patron's creatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the theatrical logistics: signals from attendants, prepared whispers, and rehearsed short answers. The social mechanics maintain the farce and assure the patron appears omniscient and gracious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperance as a principal means to health
rubrics_metrics.description: Temperance is a preservative of Health that may produce many of the same effects as Exercise and can supply its place where opportunities for exercise are wanting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperance prevents superfluities, gives nature full play, and can avert or starve growing distempers. It's presented as often preferable to internal medicines and as accessible to all ranks without expense or interruption to business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise is essential to preservation of the body
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise is absolutely necessary for the preservation of the human body; it throws off superfluities, clears the vessels, promotes circulation, and dissipates growing distempers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, prefer bodily labour and hunting-style subsistence for longevity and health; the essay contrasts active life with the ailments of luxury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dietary rule: make your whole repast out of one dish
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your whole Repast out of one Dish. If you indulge in a second, avoid drinking any thing strong till you have finished your meal; at the same time abstain from all Sauces, or at least such as are not the most plain and simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-dish meals reduce variety that provokes excess and artificial appetites. Avoiding strong drink until after the meal and minimizing sauces helps prevent gluttony and digestive disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Days of abstinence
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Man should have his Days of Abstinence, according as his Constitution will permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic abstinence relieves nature, prepares the body for hardship, can kill a sickness in embryo, and helps restore tone. The rule is flexible to constitution but recommended as a regular practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule for drinking (Sir William Temple's four glasses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first Glass for myself, the second for my Friends, the third for good Humour, and the fourth for mine Enemies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a moderation heuristic for wine consumption: limit yourself to three socially or personally positive glasses; the fourth is dangerous and associated with hostility or excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperance leads to longevity (Cornaro example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example of Lewis Cornaro who, by an exact course of temperance after forty, recovered health and lived to publish his treatise and reach advanced old age comfortably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical exemplars: temperance and sobriety commonly accompany long life among philosophers and sages; this is evidence-based persuasion rather than an explicit procedural rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend and reciprocate in friendship and love; avoid indifferent behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: To be grave to a man's mirth, unattentive to his discourse, or to interrupt either with something that argues a disinclination to be entertained by him, is extremely disagreeable. In love, a little tenderness of behaviour or regard to shew an inclination to please would make husbands entirely at ease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglecting to show simple attentions in friendship or marriage causes disproportionate distress; therefore practise responsiveness, avoid affected indifference, and be careful of actions that appear secretive or dallying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with mercurial/variable friends
rubrics_metrics.description: Some friends are mercurial—by turns the best friends and the greatest strangers; their variable attendance causes suffering and requires reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record patterns (seasons of sociability) and, if possible, encourage consistency; when addressing variability, aim to reform manners gently or adjust expectations rather than retaliate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize profession-shaped conversational faults
rubrics_metrics.description: A man's business or profession gives a cast to his mind and habits of conversation: the mathematician demands demonstration, the schoolman loves definitions, the physician and divine dictate with authority, and the lawyer raises disputable cases out of everything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that training breeds conversational predispositions; this recognition helps temper one's reactions and calibrate expectations when conversing across professional cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disputes; rules for arguing well
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid Disputes as much as possible. If obliged to argue: give your reasons with the utmost Coolness and Modesty; be neither dogmatical nor overbearing; make a graceful retreat if pinched; use the Socratic way of desiring information; ask what your opinion would be with your adversary's biases; do not fall into passion; aim for information rather than victory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific recommended behaviours: (1) prefer improving others' notions to contradicting them; (2) maintain coolness and modesty to make an impression; (3) admit you may be better informed to withdraw gracefully; (4) consider adversary's background to curb anger; (5) act as moderator where possible to gain esteem; (6) when victorious, do not push the victory too far—show generosity.
